lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: representing distributions with dot plots, histograms, and box plots

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

items.prompt: Row 1 has 12 yes and 8 no. Fraction of row 1 saying yes?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 8x + 45, where x is measured in kilometre travelleds and y in litres of fuel. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional litres of fuel is associated with 8 more kilometre travelleds.
Each additional kilometre travelled is associated with an increase of about 8 litres of fuel.
The predicted value is 8 litres of fuel when x is 0.
Each additional kilometre travelled causes an increase of exactly 8 litres of fuel.

items.prompt: Towns with more fire engines report more fire damage. What conclusion is justified?
choices: Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A data set records 4, 9, 13, 6, 10. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 8.4, median 8
mean 8, median 9
mean 9, median 8.4
mean 8.4, median 9

items.prompt: A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 336 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: Both the mean and the median rise sharply.
Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.
The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 9 yes, 44 no; row 2: 35 yes, 16 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 13x + 35, where x is measured in hour studieds and y in test points. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional test points is associated with 13 more hour studieds.
Each additional hour studied causes an increase of exactly 13 test points.
The predicted value is 13 test points when x is 0.
Each additional hour studied is associated with an increase of about 13 test points.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: Ice cream sales and swimming-pool admissions are strongly positively correlated across a year. What conclusion is justified?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A data set records 32, 5, 30, 13, 37, 2, 28. Give the mean and the median.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
